title: Linked groups where nobody has looked
question: Which are the largest tightly linked groups in which no member is a party to a case, the subject of an official finding, or named in a case file?
finding: 72 of the 111 groups have no member that is a party to a case, the subject of an official finding, or named in any case file. The largest is named after Intersection For The Arts: 10 members, 9 linked pairs, 12 kinds of unreviewed warning sign and $17.4 million of City money since fiscal 2019.
how: The groups of the first screen, keeping only those in which no core member is a party in the record of case outcomes, none is the subject of an official finding of its own (audit, monitoring finding, suspension or debarment, regulator’s status, penalty), and none is named in any of this project’s case files. Ranked by number of core members, then linked pairs, then City money. Built on the graph described under “The linked groups”: organizations, firms, San Francisco addresses and people (officers, registered lobbyists and consultants, officials) joined by eleven kinds of recorded link, each with its source. Public bodies, banks, utilities, insurers, law and accounting firms, universities, hospitals, office buildings, and any node tied to more than 12 others by one kind of link were removed first. A person appears only on a rare full name, in a public role on file, with a second independent record for each tie, and is always a name match. A member is called a party only if the record of case outcomes lists it as one; being named in a case file is shown separately. Groups are the connected sets that remain, or the tightly linked cores of sets larger than 40.
limits: Being linked is not being involved: nonprofits share board members, buildings and auditors all the time, and San Francisco is a small city. A group is a place to look, ranked by how many independent signs sit inside it. No finding can mean that nobody has looked or that there is nothing to find; this screen cannot tell which. Official findings are those this project has on file (Controller monitoring, audits, debarments, federal and State lists); a review that left no public record is invisible. Arts institutions and neighbourhood districts that share trustees form several of these groups, which is how such boards are usually built. Shares an officer or director (name match): board members often serve several organizations, and affiliates share leaders as a matter of course. Same street address: nonprofit centres, landlords and tenants, and fiscal sponsors share buildings. Pays (grant, contract or rent): sub-grants and specialist contractors are how programmes are delivered.
